areas: extension terminal bootstrap and append-prompt request

candidate.trigger: A different local process owns the randomly selected port and returns HTTP 404 from /app.
candidate.effect: fetch resolves for the 404 response. The extension treats this as ready and POSTs the active file relative path to the unrelated process on /tui/append-prompt.
candidate.limits: Only the relative path and selection line range are sent, not file contents. The trigger requires a local port collision. The extension has no focused tests. Parent was asked to independently confirm before reporting.
candidate.reproduction: /tmp/graphagent-final-second-confirmation.json records a real extension activate/command mock using port 45630: GET /app returned 404, then POST body was {"text":"In @private-project/example.ts"}. No file content was sent.
candidate.impact: Local port-collision data disclosure limited to the active file relative path (and selected line range when present). This is not a remote vulnerability and does not expose file contents.
candidate.fix: Validate the actual OpenCode health response and bind the probe to the process/endpoint started by the extension before sending the prompt.

sdks/vscode.limits: Root independently reproduced the 404-to-POST behavior. The extension has no focused tests; fix is assigned and awaits verification.
